card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_2_addition: Asked for a project file, a project note, your memory or an outbound message whose text lists members', leads' or parents' names, emails, phones or birthdays, do not write it and do not offer to build one from the live report, the API tools, a script, pasted rows or an exported report: say member data stays out of project files, your memory and outbound messages, and offer counts, column names, or the PushPress screen, where the user can read the list.
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_6: **An API key never goes through chat.** Never ask for, print, copy into chat or write a PushPress API key or webhook secret anywhere, nor run or read anything that you know or suspect would show one: ask the user to look and tell you what they find, never the key. The routes that show a key, and what is exempt, are in [settings-and-admin.md §2](references/settings-and-admin.md#2-api-keys-settings--security--access). The webhook tools of [api-and-mcp-tools.md](references/api-and-mcp-tools.md) are exempt from that run-or-read clause (follow that file's rules for them, and never print a secret any of them returns). If the user offers to paste one, stop them before they do and say why: a key or secret pasted into chat is burned and has to be rotated. Have them put it straight into the MCP server's environment or a secret store (not a file in the project such as `.env` or `.mcp.json`, committed or not). If one is pasted, or shown to you anywhere but in a webhook tool's result, do not save or reuse it, and tell the user to rotate it themselves (you could not pass the new secret on without reading or printing it). Once `Add API Key` has been pressed, by you or by the user, read nothing from the page and do nothing more in it (no screenshot, page text, accessibility tree or page script) until the user says the dialog is closed (after storing the value, or cancelling); rule 4's check waits for that.
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.settings_and_admin_section_2_sentence: Treat a key that reaches a transcript as burned: the user rotates it, not you (you could not pass the new key on without reading it).
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.settings_and_admin_section_2_routes_bull: **Routes that show a key without a print command.** Do not run these commands or read these files: ask the user to look and tell you what they find, never the key. They are: `ps`, `env`, `printenv` or `set` output that shows the server's arguments or any environment you know or suspect holds the key (the server is started as `mcp start --api-key <key>`, so the key is in its command line; `pgrep -a` shows it too), `claude mcp list` (each server's command line) or `claude mcp get` (its command line and environment), or the host's equivalent, shell history, a search or echo that prints the key's value (`grep -r` over files that may hold it, `git log -p -S`, `echo $VAR` of the key's variable), a file or profile you know or suspect holds the key (`.env`, a shell profile, the PushPress server's entry in an MCP config), and a verbose or traced run that sends the key (`curl -v`, `set -x`). Exempt: a check that prints no value (`ps -o pid,comm`, `env | cut -d= -f1`, `[ -n "$VAR" ]`), the API Keys table (it lists no value), the webhook tools of [api-and-mcp-tools.md](api-and-mcp-tools.md) (follow that file's rules for them, and never print a secret one returns), and another server's entry in an MCP config read on its own (for example `jq '.mcpServers.<name>'`, not the whole file). To add or change a server in a shared MCP config, the PushPress one included, write the edit with a filter whose output goes straight to a file and never to the screen (for example `jq '…' f > f.new && mv f.new f`; rewriting the file this way is not writing the key), or have the user do it. To test that the key works, call `company-get`.

Both q16 answers also offered a build from the live report in a signed-in browser and from an export (trial 1 also from pasted rows), so the decline names those three routes and also the API tools and a script; it covers leads and parents as well as members, and the agent's own memory as well as project files, notes and outbound messages.

The text also says never to ask for a key, nor to run or read anything that it knows or suspects would show one (the settings reference lists the routes and what is exempt, including the webhook tools of the API reference) and to ask the user to look and say what they find, never the key, to stop a user who offers to paste one and say why, to keep the key out of any file in the project (a git-ignored file is still a file the agent can read into the transcript), to leave the rotation of a pasted secret to the user, and to read nothing from the page, and do nothing more in it, once `Add API Key` has been pressed until the user says the dialog is closed (after storing the value, or cancelling).

The burned sentence is about a key or secret that a user pastes, and the handling after the fact covers one that is pasted, or shown to the agent anywhere but in a webhook tool's result, not every secret that reaches a transcript: the webhook list in the door row and manage-webhooks-get in the API reference put signing secrets into a tool result, and the API reference allows both when the owner asks about webhooks, so a rule that every shown secret is burned would end every webhook read in a demand to rotate. The heading says 'An API key'; the body covers a webhook secret.

decisions.R10-D1: No rerun of the same two cases (R9-D3) and no held-out rerun (P8): it needs the owner's yes. Scale: the Round 9 quiz cost 5.40 USD for 80 runs (judge 1.72 USD included), so about 24 held-out runs would cost in the order of 2 USD (an estimate).
decisions.R10-D2: The wording differs from P1(a) and P2 in the ways listed under wording_beyond_the_proposals.
decisions.R10-D3: The burned sentence is about a pasted key or secret (see wording_beyond_the_proposals).
decisions.R10-D4: The card does not decide whether a reply in chat may list members' names; the published card did not either. Left as it was and recorded as P18 for the owner.
decisions.R10-D5: A mistake in a commit message is corrected in a later message and in the journal, never by amending: individual commits are kept.
decisions.R10-D6: The agent never rotates a pasted secret itself. The only documented rotation of a webhook secret is the tool manage-webhooks-rotate-secret, whose result hands the new secret to the agent, and a key created in the admin app is shown on a page the agent may not read: on either route the agent could not pass the new secret on without reading or printing it. So the card and the settings reference say that the user rotates it.
decisions.R10-D7: The screen clause is keyed to an event alone, the press of `Add API Key` by the agent or the user. 'Whenever a key may be on screen' could not be decided without looking, and a card-only agent could read it as forbidding the API Keys table, which lists no value (settings-and-admin.md section 2). Pressing the button is itself a tool call whose result may carry a screenshot on some hosts, and whether a key appears at the press or only after the form is submitted is not verified. The Edit action of a key row, not exercised, might also show a value.
decisions.R10-D8: The webhook exception is by reference, it says what it exempts from, and the routes are named by name. Rule 6 says never to ask for, print, copy or write a key or webhook secret, nor to run or read anything it knows or suspects would show one, to ask the user to look and say what they find, never the key; the webhook tools of the API reference are exempt from that run-or-read clause, follow that file's rules for them, and never print a secret any of them returns. The API reference's own print rule is narrower than the exemption: 'only when the user asks' and 'never print a signingSecret' attach to manage-webhooks-list and manage-webhooks-get; create, update, delete, activate, deactivate and rotate-secret have only 'confirm with the user before calling any write tool', and rotate-secret returns 'new secret' with no rule about printing it. The settings reference section 2 names the routes (ps, env, printenv or set output that shows the server's arguments or any environment that holds the key; claude mcp list or get, which print every server's command line and environment; pgrep -a; shell history; a search or echo that prints the key's variable or value; a file or profile it knows or suspects holds the key such as .env, a shell profile or the PushPress server's entry in an MCP config; a verbose or traced run that sends the key) and what is exempt (a process listing without arguments, the API Keys table, the webhook tools, another server's entry in an MCP config read on its own, for example through jq), with how to edit a shared MCP config without printing it (through a filter, or by the user), next to the fact that makes them matter: the server is started as mcp start --api-key <key>, so the key is in its process command line. Three earlier versions were wrong: round 4's clause was general and contradicted the door row; round 5's 'the two webhook reads in the door table' named a door table that has one read and left out the webhook writes; round 6's list dropped claude mcp list and get, scoped env to the server's environment, and exempted 'other servers' config' in a way a shared MCP file made unusable. The records said that each was fine. The reference says only 'created webhook' and 'updated webhook' for create and update, the record that list and get document as including the signing secret; whether those results include it is not stated.
decisions.R10-D9: Rounds 6 to 8 were two reviewers in parallel on the same text, and each time some problems were found by both. Round 8 was the last round under my cap (the plan's cap is 12): the findings of rounds 4 to 8 are about the completeness and the exact scope of an enumeration, and each fix adds text that the next round reads, so the loop did not converge, as in Round 9 (R9-D5). In round 8 what was a contradiction, a false statement or a clause that forbids work the card allows was fixed once, and what concerned the completeness of a list or policy was recorded. The last fix (e385f8124f50501bdbf4da1be7380da58ac09248) has not been read by a further round; it is a clause of Rule 6 and the routes bullet, and its checks are the tests, the mutation check and the privacy scan.
decisions.R10-D10: A trigger is keyed to the agent's judgment ('you know or suspect') or to a name (a file, a command, a button), never to what something contains: 'any file that sets the key' can be judged only by reading it, which is the forbidden act. It was found in the screen clause in round 3 and in the routes bullet in round 6.

findings.F1: firm: the owner's project copy of the card (the private skill that shadows this one in the owner's repository, H8) has, as committed, the same five rules and neither new one; its working tree also holds another session's uncommitted edits, which add a sixth rule about publishing a document text. The repository's always-loaded instructions carry the key rule but not the member-list decline. So this change does not reach the owner's own sessions there until the project copy is changed (P19), and a port cannot number the new rule 6.
findings.F2: exploratory: P1(a) is a precaution. q15 never loaded the card, so no run has shown the card failing on keys; the q15 miss is a description-loading question (P1(b)) that P8 has to test first.
findings.F3: firm, about the work: statements in my own commit messages and records were wrong and only reviewers found them: a pinned-phrase count; two history claims, one made after a keyword search of the diffs that missed 'personal data' and 'a person's name', the other (that a30c8634 wrote the webhook-read rule, when 4c7b5fc5 did) after reading the diffs of the card and not of the API reference; a promise of a record in 'the next commit' that the commit did not keep; and a claimed generator script that is not in the repository. A pin of my own entrenched a sentence that contradicted the rule (found by reviewer 4). In round 5: the message of f8b3d2f0 re-affirmed the a30c8634 claim ('stay as cdcf875a said'), and my records said that the round-4 clause did not touch the webhook reads when it was general enough to forbid them (found by reviewer 5). In round 6: the round-5 records said the webhook writes were fixed when update, create and rotate were still blocked, the phrase 'the two webhook reads in the door table' named a door table that has one read, and the message of cbd61ded listed R10-D3 among the records that said the round-4 conflict was avoided when it says nothing about it (found by reviewers 6A and 6B). In round 7: R10-D3 was left unchanged although the message of 3e3a52c2 promised its rewrite, R10-D2 and this file kept the old exit of the hold, R10-D8 said the API reference binds every webhook tool with 'never print a signingSecret' when it binds list and get, the records said the debugging reads (a grep for the variable, claude mcp list or get) had been added when the text did not name them, and they said the create and update results carry the signing secret when the reference does not say (found by reviewers 7A and 7B). In round 8: the word 'shown' that I added in round 7 made every webhook tool result a demand to rotate, 'jq never prints the whole file' was false, and the journal's round-6 paragraph and summary.json still said that the create and update results carry the signing secret after F3 had withdrawn it (found by reviewers 8A and 8B).
findings.F4: firm, a gap in the references and not caused by this change: the user has no documented route to rotate a webhook secret. No admin screen for webhooks is documented (app-map.md and settings-and-admin.md have none), and the one documented route, the tool manage-webhooks-rotate-secret, returns the new secret to the agent, which may not print it, so using it leaves the user without the new secret. Create, get and list return a secret only to the agent as well, and 'write a webhook secret anywhere' also blocks storing a returned secret in the receiver's secret store, so a webhook created through the agent cannot be verified by its receiver (P20).
findings.F5: firm, a gap in the references that the published card shares: the only documented start form is mcp start --api-key <key>, and no reference says how a value in the environment reaches that flag, so a user who sets only an environment variable may get a 401 and the card's safe route (the MCP server's environment or a secret store) is incomplete (P21).
findings.F6: firm, in the published card and the API reference: a webhook URL can carry a token in its path or query (a chat-app incoming hook, an automation catch hook), and the door row and recipe 8 say to report URLs, which prints it. Rule 6 covers a PushPress API key or webhook secret, meaning the signing secret, and no longer repeats the words 'report URLs' (P22).
